Based on my search, I can provide you with comprehensive information about the **Navy P-3**, which refers to the **Lockheed P-3 Orion**, a maritime patrol aircraft used by the U.S. Navy and other navies worldwide.

## Overview

The **P-3 Orion** is a four-engine turboprop anti-submarine and maritime surveillance aircraft developed by Lockheed. It was first fielded by the U.S. Navy in **1962** and became one of the most widely used maritime patrol aircraft in the world.

## Key Specifications

| Feature | Specification |
|---------|-------------|
| **Engines** | 4 × Allison T56-A-14 turboprops |
| **Shaft Horsepower** | 4,600 SHP per engine |
| **Propeller Diameter** | 13.5 feet (4-blade Hamilton Standard) |
| **Maximum Speed** | 466 mph (dash speed) |
| **Endurance** | Up to 16 hours |
| **Maximum Altitude** | ~32,000 ft (28,000 ft RVSM limited) |
| **Crew** | Up to 12 personnel |

## Primary Missions

- **Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW)** – Using sonobuoys, magnetic anomaly detector (MAD) "stinger" tail boom, and torpedoes/depth charges
- **Anti-Surface Warfare (ASuW)** – Armed with Harpoon missiles, mines, and other weapons on 10 wing hard-points
- **Maritime Patrol & Surveillance**
- **Search and Rescue (SAR)**
- **Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR)**

## Current Status (U.S. Navy)

The U.S. Navy has been transitioning from the P-3C Orion to the **P-8A Poseidon** (based on the Boeing 737). As of recent updates:

- The last active-duty U.S. Navy P-3C squadrons completed their final deployments around **2019**
- As of **October 2025**, only **six** active U.S. Navy P-3 Orions remain in service:
  - **VX-30** (test squadron): 4 aircraft
  - **VXS-1** (scientific development squadron): 2 aircraft

## International Operators

The P-3 continues to serve with numerous international navies and air forces, including:

| Country | Status |
|---------|--------|
| **Argentina** | Recently acquired P-3Cs from Norway (2024-2025) |
| **Canada** | CP-140 Aurora (customized variant), being phased out |
| **Germany** | Retired in 2025; transitioning to P-8A Poseidon |
| **Greece** | Modernizing P-3B fleet (first flight September 2025) |
| **Japan** | Transitioning to domestic P-1 patrol aircraft |
| **Norway** | Sold remaining aircraft to Argentina |
| **Portugal** | Operating P-3C CUP+ and ex-German aircraft |

## Design Features

- **Shortened fuselage** (7 feet shorter than the L-188 Electra commercial airliner) to save weight
- **MAD (Magnetic Anomaly Detector)** tail boom for submarine detection
- **Bomb bay** for torpedoes and depth charges
- **External hardpoints** for missiles and other ordnance

## NASA & Scientific Use

NASA operates P-3B aircraft as airborne science platforms for atmospheric research, earth science, and other experiments. The NASA P-3 is similar in size and basic furnishings to Navy P-3 aircraft but extensively modified for research missions.

---

Sources:
1. https://airbornescience.nasa.gov/sites/default/files/P-3B%20Experimenter%20Handbook%20548-HDBK-0001.pdf
2. https://www.p3orion.nl/news.html
3. https://www.twz.com/27565/the-navys-last-active-duty-p-3c-patrol-squadron-is-on-its-final-deployment
4. https://www.naval-technology.com/news/argentina-enriches-naval-surveillance-with-acquisition-of-p-3-orion/
5. https://airandspace.si.edu/air-and-space-quarterly/issue-13/orion-p3
6. https://news.lockheedmartin.com/2019-05-17-Hellenic-Navy-Receives-First-Modernized-P-3-Orion-Maritime-Patrol-Aircraft
